scope: Independent read-only review of the frozen four Swift sources, three production diffs, six new test definitions and necessary existing owner APIs. Source/hash review only; no grammar, test, SDK, Keychain/TLS/device, Git or cloud execution. No canonical source edits.

resolvedConfirmedFinding.confirmedBehavior: The v1 catch returned unavailable(fallbackError) even when the preceding independent normal-load observation also failed. Its separate userDataError was dropped. This was an error-fact loss, not signing restoration or a successful observation. Author confirmed it.
resolvedConfirmedFinding.v2Fix: Only the catch changed: classify the original fallback error before wrapping; if userDataError exists, retain both in ObservationFailures(installedMaterial: fallbackError, normalUserData: userDataError). The original materialFailure remains separately retained, and recovery context remains nested in the original fallback error when supplied. Cancellation stays a separate preceding catch.
resolvedConfirmedFinding.status: closed by source review; no execution claim

reviewedBoundaries.boundary: Live Vault lease before successful early returns
reviewedBoundaries.finding: observeCurrentProcess and limited revalidateSigningMaterials share validatedObservationContext. It checks cancellation, reads the same locked Journal, calls actual vault.lease and compares current namespace/generation before nil/unsubmitted/same-process cached observation can return. Existing Vault.current rereads exact Keychain manifest bytes; actual lease.verify checks the current key, chain/profile validity and bounded inputs. No retained SecKey is treated as current authorization.

The Session stores only max(createdAt) and min(expiresAt) from the actual verified connect profile collection, bounds the count, requires finite ordered dates, and validates the current clock before foreground observation. It does not claim to reverify all original certificate dates, all post-connect application bytes, or online Apple revocation.

Session and Coordinator retain their existing busy admission guards. Any observed non-cancellation material failure clears vault/coordinator/access/profileValidity before awaiting independent normal-load work; cancellation after this point cannot restore signing. Pre-admission cancellation checks occur before local owner/configuration mutations. Current cancellation is not converted into missing materials or automatic recovery.

Only the existing material-error whitelist may enter recoveryConnection. Storage/Keychain read failures, read races, limits and cancellation remain typed. Recovery construction loads an actual eligible Journal phase with namespace and any supplied peer binding, uses the same journal and contains no Vault/Namespace/signing proof. Foreground/boot never calls the authenticated network entry. Explicit recovery retains the prior Lookup-only or safe cleanup behavior.

reviewedBoundaries.boundary: Completed remote facts and failed local acknowledgement
reviewedBoundaries.finding: recoverExplicitly still stores the real completed Coordinator.Recovery before the post-recovery observation/publication catch. Any later failure wraps it in RecoveryFailed(completedRecovery: completed) alongside materialFailure/observationError. No local status write failure is recast as an unsubmitted remote operation. publish still invalidates capabilities and requires reload on commitDurabilityUnknown.

reviewedBoundaries.boundary: Stale signing status after failed writes
reviewedBoundaries.finding: status() compares the last acknowledged status access with the actually retained access. On mismatch it returns an unavailable in-memory projection with the prior observedAt, not an invented durable publication or fresh observation. The failed write error remains in Unavailable.statusPersistenceError and Owner classifies it as local storage. Configuration/recovery state is not silently rewritten.

reviewedBoundaries.boundary: DEBUG owned application and product routing
reviewedBoundaries.finding: Only DEBUG initializers can supply currentApplicationRoot; production init sets it nil and uses Bundle.main. Configuration JSON has no root/proof field. The owned path still passes actual ApplicationMaterialVerifier, Vault.resume/lease/identity checks; phase requiring installed/current-process observation throws ownedApplicationIsNotCurrentProcess before readCurrentProcess/noteCurrentProcessMaterial. It does not manufacture a proof from a Bool or raw fixture root.

reviewedBoundaries.boundary: Existing foreground App owner and performance
reviewedBoundaries.finding: The existing App DI owner and becameActive?bootstrap?Session?Coordinator route are retained. Initialization remains O(1), material/file operations remain on existing service actors/verifier workers, and no main-thread disk/Keychain work, new transport/store/WebView, submission timer, auto-Upload or auto-Upgrade path is introduced.

preparedValidation.note: Reviewed bodies genuinely call the actual owned verifiers/Keychain/journal/TLS fixture paths when executed. They are still definitions only; explicit loops are not extra parameter leaves. The v2 catch fix adds no artificial writer/proof/fault helper.

remaining: This change is not SDK compilation or execution evidence. The six methods are definitions only until an actual same-source App SDK batch runs.

No authentic current-process synthetic-package proof is fabricated to exercise the cache hit. The guard ordering is independently source-reviewed; the DEBUG owned root explicitly refuses that process-proof branch.

Offline revalidation detects locally known signed validity dates, actual local Keychain missing/revoked/changed publication, and current offline chain/profile verification. It cannot discover a new server-side revocation without an authorized online channel.

The original connected application material is not wholly reread or continuously monitored on each foreground. Only its already-verified profile date bounds are retained; unrelated post-connect on-disk mutations and installed certificate-chain temporal changes are not newly revalidated by those two dates.

A failed foreground leaves explicit recovery available only when an actual eligible existing journal record permits it. Safe cleanup remains candidateReady in recovery-only mode and never authorizes retirement, new signing, Upload or Upgrade.
Status has no newly inferred Apple/account/device/install authorization, kernel image authenticity, cold-launch proof, complete data preservation, autonomous scheduling or automatic renewal success.
verdict: No remaining confirmed blocker in this bounded foreground revalidation source delta. The one independently confirmed error-fact loss is closed in v2. Author may proceed with the single planned grammar check; actual same-source SDK validation remains required.
